title: Lists sort with NULL elements lowest; no `<` or `min` on lists
verdict: `list_null_order: LEAST` in sorts; list comparisons refused
description: `sort` orders lists lexicographically, a prefix first, and a NULL element below every value: `[] < [NULL] < [1] < [1, NULL] < [1, 2]` ascending, reversed descending, NULL lists first by default. `<` between lists and `min`, `max` of lists raise (`InvalidOperationError`).
reference: `list_null_order`: NULL where a NULL element decides `<`, and `GREATEST` in `ORDER BY` (#207). DuckDB puts the NULL element above every value (duckdb-R11).

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_polars` runs each expression on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the bounds of the integer width; 0.5, ±2.5, 7, 1e308, ±inf, NaN; NULL), one row at a time, and compares each row with Lean's outcome of the Substrait call under each candidate option (`substrait-check --outcomes`). Observations are Polars programs whose result is recorded as it is. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), Rust crates at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3), on macOS arm64.
